fullText:
Imagine a robot walking in a museum and mapping everything it sees.

The robot uses every camera frame to estimate where it is and build a 3D representation.

But generating a good map is hard: every small error can accumulate as the robot moves, causing the map to gradually drift out of alignment.

@robbyant_brain addresses this with LingBot-Map 2.0:

It's a model that takes video and estimates the camera's path and the scene's 3D geometry frame by frame.

This version has a new feature: Refine, and the way it works is pretty cool:

• Refine updates the geometric context the model uses to estimate the camera trajectory.

• It saves those updates to the model so it can improve existing reconstructions and use the updated geometry to process future frames.

• You can trigger Refine at any point during a run to reduce accumulated drift.

And all of this happens inside the model, without any external optimization backend.

Look at the attached demo:

• The orange path is the estimated camera trajectory before Refine.
• The cyan path shows the corrected trajectory after Refine.

This is one of the key capabilities supporting the embodied-native, general-purpose robot brain @robbyant_brain is building. Without reliable spatial memory, autonomous work over large areas and long hours isn't possible.

Here is more information about the model:

• Project page: https://t.co/6eOgPpXAmV

• Technical report: https://t.co/CLKWm7l384

• GitHub: https://t.co/boWEZ4hH1t

• Hugging Face: https://t.co/7r3UTMRwWv

The Streaming version is open source; Refine is not included.

fullText:
Great paper from Microsoft on how much coding agents over-edit.

It is widely assumed that coding agents over-edit, because their patches are larger than developer patches.

This study tested that claim on 7,660 resolved GitHub Copilot CLI trajectories from 18 frontier models. Their method, Delta Residue Attribution, reverts each block of the final patch, reruns the task tests, and records whether the block was needed.

On SWE-bench Verified, most of the extra lines are tests (61%) and documentation (13%). Agent code was on average at least as necessary as developer code (0.887 vs 0.864), and 11 of 18 models left less unneeded code than developers.

About 11% of an agent's code units were still unneeded, and 89% of those changed behavior. Code necessity had no relation to resolve rate on SWE-bench Verified and a negative one on DeepSWE (Spearman -0.59).

Pruning with only the tests the agent can see removed most of the unneeded code, and 89% of pruned patches still resolved the task.

fullText:
有人把180B的Qwen 3.8 Flash Next装进了一台只有64GB内存的Mac M4 Max里，推理速度达到56 tok/s

基于刚刚开源的本地推理引擎Magnitude最新版实现的，跑Qwen 3.8 Flash Next 180B-A6B，2-bit量化，64K上下文

过去想在本地流畅跑180B级的模型，得花1–2万美元买工作站

核心是利用了现代稀疏MoE模型的特点，180B参数里，每个Token实际只激活约6B，97%的参数在每一步都在摸鱼

所以Magnitude把注意力层和高频使用的专家权重留在高速内存中，其余专家权重放在SSD上，按需加载

但直接从SSD读取权重会很慢，所以还做了四项优化：

第一，根据专家复用频率进行缓存排序，将高频专家保留在高速内存中，减少磁盘读取

第二，预测后续Token需要的专家，提前预取权重，减少GPU等待

第三，跨层调度NVMe直接读取，绕过操作系统Swap机制，让数据读取与计算尽可能并行，全程纯只读，不产生闪存擦写损耗

第四、优化长提示词的Prefill阶段，每层冷专家尽量只读取一次，避免冲掉解码所需的热点缓存

体验上也做得非常彻底，零配置自动调优，首次启动自动检测硬件、提前预测每个模型的生成速度，并针对你的芯片自动调优算子，速度比Ollama快2倍以上

支持Apple Silicon、NVIDIA、AMD、Intel以及纯CPU运行，可桌面客户端、CLI和Docker部署

fullText:
Knowledge Structures — Recent Developments in Theory and Application (Textbook in Advanced Mathematical Psychology): https://t.co/GPjDEOXrSA

#mathematics 

𝔹𝕠𝕠𝕜 𝕠𝕧𝕖𝕣𝕧𝕚𝕖𝕨 𝕗𝕣𝕠𝕞 𝔸𝕞𝕒𝕫𝕠𝕟:

“Founded in 1985 by Jean-Claude Falmagne and Jean-Paul Doignon, Knowledge Structure Theory (KST) constitutes a rigorous and current mathematical theory for the representation and the assessment of human knowledge. The seminal work of these authors initiated a highly active research strand with an ever-growing literature, mostly scattered across various technical journals. Starting from a concise but comprehensive introduction to its foundations, this volume provides a state-of-the-art review of KST. For the first time the volume brings together the most important theoretical developments and extensions of the last decade and presents new areas of application beyond education, with contributions by key researchers in the field. Among the important advances covered by this book are (1) a comprehensive treatment of probabilistic models in KST; (2) polytomous extensions of the theory; (3) KST-based psychological diagnostics and neuropsychological assessment; (4) the representation and assessment of cognitive skills in problem solving, as well as procedural skills. In addition, this book also includes an overview of available software for the application of KST.”

fullText:
Brian Chesky used to ask Airbnb candidates if they'd take the job with a year left to live:

"I interviewed the first 300 employees at Airbnb, which people think I'm really neurotic, and that may also be true... I used to ask them, 'If you had a year left to live, would you take this job?' "I really wanted people to think about that. That was enough time for you to do something you really cared about. And the answer doesn't have to be this company. And I say, 'Fine, if what you're meant to do is to travel... you should just do that. Don't come here. Go do that.'"

"Two men are laying bricks. Somebody comes up to the first man and says, 'What are you doing?' He says, 'I'm building a wall.' He asks the other guy, 'What are you doing?' He says, 'I'm building a cathedral.'"

"There is a job, and then there's a calling. And we want to hire people that aren't just looking for jobs. They're looking for a calling. And that's kind of the first value, and that's champion the mission."

@bchesky at Stanford, 2014
